correctness.rationale: The left regular action decomposes into the irreducible Fourier blocks with multiplicities 1,1,2,…,2. One tap is invertible; for two, left translation reduces to aI+bL_h and the largest possible eigenspace has dimension p, attained at an involution. For three taps in one coset the prime Fourier theorem gives nullity at most 4, with equality at U(z)=(z−ζ)(z−ζ²); its three coefficients are nonzero. In the 2+1 split the determinant D=U(z)U(z⁻¹)−V(z)V(z⁻¹) is supported on 0,±d, is nonzero, and has at most two prime-frequency zeros. Nontrivial zeros pair under inversion; a zero at 1 uses one slot and the singleton prevents both linear characters vanishing. The total nullity is at most 2. For four taps, the one-coset nullity is at most 6. In the 3+1 split Cauchy–Davenport gives at least four distinct nonzero differences among six ordered differences, so a singleton difference makes D nonzero. At most six Fourier roots and the same paired-root and linear-block accounting give total nullity at most 6. In the 2+2 split no 2×2 block can vanish, since a binomial cannot vanish at both distinct frequencies in its pair. A nonzero D has at most four roots and gives total nullity at most 4 even if both linear characters vanish. If D is identically zero the 2×2 blocks all have rank one, giving rank at least p−1. The product (δ_e−δ_r)*(δ_e−δ_s) has exactly four distinct nonzero taps and gives rank p−1. The weakest intermediate comparison 2p−6≥p−1 holds at and above p=5. These arguments apply to arbitrary complex coefficients and exact support sizes.
residual_risks: The reproduction uses exact characteristic-zero cyclotomic arithmetic for the displayed witnesses at p=5,7,11,13,17, not for arbitrary inputs or primes. The all-prime lower bounds follow from the reviewed proof using the prime Fourier theorem and Cauchy–Davenport.

value.rationale: The natural exact-support analogue of group uncertainty is not monotone: the three-tap minimum rises over the two-tap minimum by p−4, then the four-tap minimum drops by p−3. The growing gaps and the all-prime mixed-support sharp bound distinguish this from a finite example or a product-bound corollary. The first four levels show both changes with no arbitrary slice in p.
residual_risks: No extremizer classification or larger-support profile is claimed.
